Route from published declarations, without loading or inspecting data.

docs.title: ModeVerdict dataclass
docs.text: Declaration-level applicability and parameters required for this input.

docs.title: SGAConfig dataclass
docs.text: Configuration for the SGA search algorithm.

docs.title: aic_ratio class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
aic_ratio: float = 1.0

AIC penalty ratio.

docs.title: autograd_train_epochs class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
autograd_train_epochs: int = 1000

Maximum training epochs for the auto-trained FieldModel. Only used when use_autograd=True and field_model is None.

docs.title: autograd_train_lr class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
autograd_train_lr: float = 0.001

Learning rate for the auto-trained FieldModel. Only used when use_autograd=True and field_model is None.

docs.title: autograd_train_patience class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
autograd_train_patience: int | None = None

Early-stopping patience for the auto-trained FieldModel (epochs without validation improvement). None (default) disables early stopping, so the surrogate trains the full autograd_train_epochs budget — the v1 / paper reference semantics (sgapde/metann.py fixed-step training, no early stop). Requires autograd_train_val_ratio > 0 (there is no validation signal to monitor otherwise). Only used when use_autograd=True and field_model is None; ignored in finite-diff mode (same handling as autograd_train_epochs).

docs.title: autograd_train_val_ratio class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
autograd_train_val_ratio: float = 0.0

Fraction of data held out for validation while auto-training the FieldModel. 0.0 (default) trains on ALL data — the v1 / paper reference semantics (full-data training, no val split). Set > 0 only when using autograd_train_patience for early stopping. Only used when use_autograd=True and field_model is None; ignored in finite-diff mode (same handling as autograd_train_epochs).

docs.title: constants class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
constants: tuple[float, ...] = ()

Constant leaves added to the tabular grammar, in the order given.

docs.title: d_tol class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
d_tol: float = 1.0

Tolerance step size for STRidge sweep.

docs.title: dedup_mode class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
dedup_mode: DedupMode = 'pre_prune'

Deduplication strategy for genetic offspring.

docs.title: depth class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
depth: int = 4

Maximum tree depth for each term.

docs.title: field_model class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
field_model: FieldModel | None = None

Optional pre-trained FieldModel surrogate (skips auto-training when use_autograd=True). Must have matching coord_names / field_names. Ignored when use_autograd=False.

docs.title: functions class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
functions: tuple[str, ...] = ()

Unary functions added to the tabular grammar, in the order given.

docs.title: lam class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
lam: float = 0.0

Ridge lambda (0 = OLS).

docs.title: maxit class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
maxit: int = 10

Max steps of the inner per-candidate STRidge tolerance sweep (train_sweep in sga/train.py).

docs.title: normalize class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
normalize: int = 2

Column norm order for STRidge normalization.

docs.title: num class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
num: int = 20

Population size (number of PDE candidates).

docs.title: p_cro class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
p_cro: float = 0.5

Crossover probability between PDEs.

docs.title: p_mute class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
p_mute: float = 0.3

Mutation probability per node.

docs.title: p_rep class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
p_rep: float = 1.0

Replace probability (chance of replacing a term).

docs.title: p_var class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
p_var: float = 0.5

Probability that a node is a variable (vs. operator).

docs.title: restart_interval class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
restart_interval: int | None = None

Number of committed generations between population re-draws.

docs.title: seed class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
seed: int = 0

Random seed for reproducibility.

docs.title: str_iters class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
str_iters: int = 10

STRidge internal iterations per tolerance level.

docs.title: target_lhs_order class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
target_lhs_order: int

Time-derivative target order, matching dataset.lhs_order.

docs.title: training_dtype class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
training_dtype: TrainingDtype | None

Floating precision the auto-trained FieldModel is trained in: None (default) trains in the dataset's dtype; "float32" or "float64" names one. The trained surrogate is cast back to the dataset's dtype, so SGA's autograd terminals are computed in that dtype whatever the training precision. Only used when use_autograd=True and field_model is None. The finite-difference and tabular modes train no surrogate and refuse any value other than None.

docs.title: use_autograd class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
use_autograd: bool = False

Derivative source for the Layer 2 terminals (u_x, u_t): with autograd, SGA trains (or reuses) a FieldModel surrogate and reads them through AutogradProvider; otherwise they come from finite differences. The facade spells the two settings derivatives="autograd" and derivatives="finite_diff". Layer 1 (raw u leaf) and Layer 3 (tree d / d^2 operators) are unchanged.

docs.title: width class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
width: int = 5

Maximum number of terms per PDE.

docs.title: DLGAConfig dataclass
docs.text: DLGA Stage I (constant-coefficient) configuration.

docs.title: add_rate class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
add_rate: float = 0.4

Probability that a newly built random term is appended to a candidate, from 0 to 1. The term is added only if the candidate is below max_modules and does not already contain it.

docs.title: auto_upgrade_threshold class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
auto_upgrade_threshold: float

Reserved for the planned mode="auto" escalation: the best NMSE above which the search would hand over to an adaptive, variable-coefficient stage. It has no effect today, because "constant" is the only implemented mode, and the 1e-3 default is an untuned placeholder.

docs.title: crossover_rate class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
crossover_rate: float = 0.8

Probability that a pair of surviving candidates exchanges one term during crossover, from 0 to 1. Survivors are paired off in order, and each pair either swaps one randomly chosen term or passes through unchanged.

docs.title: delete_rate class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
delete_rate: float = 0.5

Probability that one term is dropped from a candidate, from 0 to 1. A candidate that is down to a single term is left unchanged. The draw is independent of add_rate, so one candidate can gain and lose a term in the same generation.

docs.title: epsilon class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
epsilon: float = 0.001

Complexity penalty in the genetic fitness NMSE + epsilon * length, where length is the total number of tokens across the candidate's terms. Raise it to push the search toward shorter equations; the useful value is problem- dependent, and the packaged presets span 1e-6 to 1e-3.

docs.title: genes_prob class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
genes_prob: float = 0.6

Probability, from 0 to 1, of adding one more term while a random candidate equation is built. Generation stops once the candidate reaches max_modules terms.

docs.title: lhs_auto_select class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
lhs_auto_select: bool = False

When False, every candidate is fitted against the time derivative of the order target_lhs_order names (u_t for 1, u_tt for 2) and no other. When True, every candidate is fitted against both u_t and u_tt, as the original DLGA-PDE code does, and the branch with the lower NMSE is kept (the original code compares raw MSE); the returned law's left-hand side can then be the order the dataset does not declare. A fit given a sketch uses the left-hand side the sketch states and does not read this flag.

docs.title: library class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
library: list[str]

Ordered vocabulary of tokens that candidate terms are built from, defaulting to ["u", "u_x", "u_xx", "u_xxx"]. Each term is a product of tokens drawn from this list, and the ordering matters: one of the mutation operators shifts a token to an adjacent entry. On a grid whose spatial axes are x and y, kd.Model builds the default over both axes, u, u_x, u_xx, u_xxx, u_y, u_yy, u_yyy.

docs.title: max_module_length class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
max_module_length: int = 5

Maximum number of tokens multiplied together inside a single term.

docs.title: max_modules class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
max_modules: int = 5

Maximum number of additive terms allowed in one candidate equation.

docs.title: mode class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
mode: Literal['constant', 'adaptive', 'auto']

Coefficient mode of the search; only "constant" (constant-coefficient equations) is implemented. The values "adaptive" and "auto" pass configuration validation but raise NotImplementedError when the algorithm is constructed.

docs.title: mutation_rate class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
mutation_rate: float = 0.4

Probability that a mutation shifts one factor of one term along library, from 0 to 1. The shift is to an adjacent entry, except for a factor sitting at the first entry, which is redrawn from the whole library.

docs.title: partial_prob class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
partial_prob: float = 0.6

Probability, from 0 to 1, of extending a randomly built term with one more factor. The term stops growing once it reaches max_module_length.

docs.title: pop_size class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
pop_size: int = 400

Number of candidate equations in each generation of the genetic search, which is also how many candidates the platform evaluates per iteration.

docs.title: seed class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
seed: int = 0

Random seed of the genetic search: it seeds the generator behind the initial population and every crossover, mutation, add and delete draw, and is also forwarded to the surrogate network's training. Runs differing only in this value explore different candidates.

docs.title: solver class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
solver: Literal['svd_null_space', 'ols'] = 'svd_null_space'

Solver used to fit each candidate's coefficients against the left-hand side: "svd_null_space" takes the null space of the augmented system (total least squares), "ols" uses ordinary least squares.

docs.title: surrogate_activation class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
surrogate_activation: Literal["tanh", "sin", "relu"] = (
    DLGA_NN_1.activation
)

Activation applied after each hidden layer of the fitted network: tanh, sin, or relu. The default sin stays smooth under the repeated differentiation the search relies on, which relu does not.

docs.title: surrogate_hidden_sizes class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
surrogate_hidden_sizes: list[int]

Widths of the hidden layers in the neural network fitted to the field data, one hidden layer per entry (default five layers of 50 units). The search differentiates this network for the derivatives it scores, so its capacity bounds their accuracy.

docs.title: surrogate_lr class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
surrogate_lr: float = DLGA_NN_1.lr

Learning rate of the Adam optimizer used to fit the network to the field data.

docs.title: surrogate_max_epochs class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
surrogate_max_epochs: int = DLGA_NN_1.max_epochs

Maximum number of epochs to spend fitting the network, one full-batch Adam step per epoch. It trades run time against derivative accuracy: dropping the default 50000 to a few thousand finishes much sooner with coarser derivatives.

docs.title: surrogate_patience class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
surrogate_patience: int | None = DLGA_NN_1.patience

Number of consecutive epochs without validation-loss improvement after which the fit stops early. None, the default, disables early stopping and runs the full surrogate_max_epochs budget; other values need surrogate_val_ratio above 0 to take effect.

docs.title: surrogate_restore_best class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
surrogate_restore_best: bool = DLGA_NN_1.restore_best

If True, the weights from the epoch with the lowest validation loss are restored at the end of the fit instead of keeping the last epoch's weights. Has no effect when surrogate_val_ratio is 0, since there is no validation loss to rank epochs by.

docs.title: surrogate_val_ratio class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
surrogate_val_ratio: float = DLGA_NN_1.val_ratio

Fraction of the samples held out to measure validation loss while fitting the network, from 0 up to but not including 1. Setting it to 0 trains on every sample and leaves surrogate_patience and surrogate_restore_best with no signal to act on.

docs.title: target_lhs_order class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
target_lhs_order: int = 1

Set to the dataset's left-hand-side order; 2 for u_tt.

docs.title: training_dtype class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
training_dtype: TrainingDtype | None

Floating precision the network is trained in: None, the default, trains in the dataset's dtype; "float32" or "float64" names one. The trained network is cast back to the dataset's dtype, so the search differentiates and scores it in that dtype whatever the training precision. On float64 data, "float32" shortens training on GPUs whose float64 arithmetic is slow. The value is part of a stored surrogate's identity, so a network trained in one precision does not serve a configuration that names another.

docs.title: burgers_preset classmethod
docs.text:
burgers_preset(**overrides: Any) -> DLGAConfig

DLGAConfig for the Burgers equation (epsilon=1e-3).

docs.title: chafee_preset classmethod
docs.text:
chafee_preset(**overrides: Any) -> DLGAConfig

DLGAConfig for Chafee-Infante (epsilon=1e-5).

docs.title: kdv_preset classmethod
docs.text:
kdv_preset(**overrides: Any) -> DLGAConfig

DLGAConfig for the KdV equation (epsilon=1e-6).

docs.title: kg_preset classmethod
docs.text:
kg_preset(**overrides: Any) -> DLGAConfig

DLGAConfig for the Klein-Gordon equation (u_tt LHS, epsilon=1e-3).

docs.title: wave_preset classmethod
docs.text:
wave_preset(**overrides: Any) -> DLGAConfig

DLGAConfig for the wave equation (u_tt LHS, epsilon=1e-3).

docs.title: DiscoverConfig dataclass
docs.text: Configuration for a DISCOVER (RL + optional PINN) search run.

docs.title: attention class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
attention: bool = False

When True, the controller applies additive (Bahdanau) attention over a sliding window of its own recent outputs before producing token logits. The window length is attn_length.

docs.title: attn_length class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
attn_length: int = 10

Length of the attention window, in past controller steps. It has no effect when attention is False.

docs.title: baseline class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
baseline: str = 'R_e'

Value subtracted from the rewards in the policy-gradient loss. "R_e" (the default) uses the risk-seeking reward quantile itself, "ewma_R" a moving average of the mean kept reward, and "combined" the quantile plus a moving average of the gap between the two.

docs.title: batch_size class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
batch_size: int = 16

Number of candidate expressions sampled per search iteration, and the batch the policy-gradient update is computed from; larger batches give a steadier signal at more compute per iteration. On tabular data, kd.Model defaults to 500 with epsilon=0.05 to retain multiple reward-bearing samples after invalid candidates are removed.

docs.title: diagnostic_scaffold class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
diagnostic_scaffold: bool = False

Attach the diagnostic scaffold prior, which restricts sampling in the first search cycle to a root token from diagnostic_scaffold_root_tokens whose two branches draw on disjoint token sets. Off by default; True also requires DISCOVER_ENABLE_DIAGNOSTICS=1 in the environment, because the scaffold builds an assumed equation shape into the search.

docs.title: diagnostic_scaffold_diffusion_tokens class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
diagnostic_scaffold_diffusion_tokens: tuple[str, ...] = ()

Token names the scaffold keeps to the left branch of the root: each one is excluded from sampling while the right branch is filled. Read only when diagnostic_scaffold is True, and a name also listed as neutral is exempt.

docs.title: diagnostic_scaffold_neutral_tokens class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
diagnostic_scaffold_neutral_tokens: tuple[str, ...] = ()

Token names the scaffold never excludes, so they stay samplable in both branches even when they also appear in the diffusion or reaction list. Read only when diagnostic_scaffold is True; a name shared with diagnostic_scaffold_root_tokens is rejected.

docs.title: diagnostic_scaffold_reaction_tokens class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
diagnostic_scaffold_reaction_tokens: tuple[str, ...] = ()

Token names the scaffold keeps to the right branch of the root: each one is excluded from sampling while the left branch is filled. Read only when diagnostic_scaffold is True, and a name also listed as neutral is exempt.

docs.title: diagnostic_scaffold_root_tokens class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
diagnostic_scaffold_root_tokens: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "add",
    "sub",
)

Token names the scaffold allows at the root of a sampled expression; at the first sampling step every other token is excluded, so the tree starts from one of these. Defaults to ("add", "sub") and is read only when diagnostic_scaffold is True; a set in which no name exists in the token library fails when the search is built.

docs.title: embedding_dim class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
embedding_dim: int = 4

Width of the learned embedding used for each categorical observation channel. It has no effect unless use_embedding is True, which replaces the one-hot inputs with embeddings of this size.

docs.title: entropy_gamma class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
entropy_gamma: float = 1.0

Per-position decay of the entropy bonus: the entropy at position t of a sampled sequence is weighted by entropy_gamma ** t. The default 1.0 weights every position equally; values below 1 concentrate the exploration bonus on the first tokens.

docs.title: entropy_weight class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
entropy_weight: float = 0.005

Weight of the entropy bonus added to the policy-gradient loss, which rewards a less peaked sampling distribution. Must be non-negative; raise it when the controller commits to one expression family too early, set 0.0 to drop the bonus.

docs.title: epsilon class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
epsilon: float = 0.1

Risk-seeking quantile: the policy-gradient update keeps the batch rewards at or above the 1 - epsilon quantile (RSPGStrategy), so a smaller value is a greedier update off fewer samples. Ties at the quantile are all kept, so the retained share can exceed epsilon (an all-equal batch keeps everything). Must lie in (0, 1]. With the R_e baseline the advantage is reward - quantile, so batch_size * epsilon must exceed 1 or the quantile is the batch maximum and the reward term of the loss is identically zero. The default 0.10 is sized for the default batch of 16; the packaged PDE presets pair 0.01-0.02 with batches of 500-1000. On tabular data, kd.Model defaults to 0.05 with a batch of 500 so multiple samples can have nonzero advantage after invalid candidates are removed. The batch_size * epsilon > 1 rule applies to the remaining valid batch.

docs.title: gamma class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
gamma: float = 0.5

Decay of the moving-average baseline: the running value keeps weight gamma and the new batch contributes 1 - gamma. In the range 0 to 1, and only read when baseline is "ewma_R" or "combined".

docs.title: initializer class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
initializer: Literal['xavier', 'zeros'] = 'xavier'

Parameter initialization scheme, either "xavier" or "zeros". "xavier" draws all parameters from a Xavier/uniform baseline; "zeros" also zeroes the LSTM cell parameters and the output bias, making the initial token distribution uniform.

docs.title: learning_rate class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
learning_rate: float = 0.001

Step size of the Adam optimizer that updates the controller network. A run resumed from a checkpoint adopts this value rather than the one saved with the checkpoint.

docs.title: library class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
library: LibraryConfig

Operator/terminal table the controller samples expression trees from. It carries three lists: operators (the function set, default ["add", "mul", "sub", "div", "sin", "cos", "diff_x", "diff2_x"]), state_vars (default ["u"]) and coord_vars (default ["x", "t"]). Library lays the tokens out in the order coord_vars, state_vars, operators, and that order fixes the token indices the controller's logits and the sampling priors address.

docs.title: magnitude_filter class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
magnitude_filter: bool = False

When True, a fit whose active coefficients include any magnitude below 5e-5 or above 1e4 is marked invalid, so it scores zero reward and is dropped from controller training. Defaults to False, which accepts a fit at any coefficient magnitude.

docs.title: max_diff_order class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
max_diff_order: int | None = 4

Highest cumulative derivative order allowed in a sampled expression; candidates above it are rejected before evaluation. Orders accumulate along a chain, so diff2_x(diff_x(u)) counts as 3, and None disables the check.

docs.title: max_length class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
max_length: int = 15

Maximum number of tokens in a sampled expression tree, default 15. The length prior forbids any operator that could not still finish the tree within this budget, so a sample never exceeds it; the same bound also caps the complexity of the frontier rows the plugin publishes.

docs.title: min_length class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
min_length: int = 2

Minimum length of a sampled expression, in tokens. The sampler is forbidden from ending an expression before this many tokens, and any candidate that still comes out shorter is rejected before evaluation.

docs.title: n_iterations class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
n_iterations: int = 2000

With pinn set, the number of search generations before the first PINN phase, which must be smaller than Model(generations=...) for any PINN phase to run; without pinn, kd.Model ignores this field and warns on a non-default value. The default 2000 is not smaller than the facade's default of 50 generations. On the standalone paths, where Model(generations=...) does not exist, it is the number of search iterations the entry point runs, one controller batch per iteration, and the length of a PINNCycleRunner cycle unless PINNConfig.cycle_n_iterations sets the later cycles.

docs.title: num_layers class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
num_layers: int = 1

Number of stacked LSTM layers in the controller. Layers beyond the first take the previous layer's hidden state as their input.

docs.title: num_units class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
num_units: int = 16

Number of hidden units in each LSTM layer of the controller. It also sets the width of the attention projections when attention is enabled.

docs.title: observe_action class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
observe_action: bool = False

When True, the token sampled at the previous step is added to the controller input, as a one-hot vector or as an embedding when use_embedding is set.

docs.title: observe_dangling class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
observe_dangling: bool = False

When True, the count of unfilled argument slots in the partial expression tree is appended to the controller input as a single numeric value. This channel is always a raw count, so use_embedding does not apply to it.

docs.title: observe_parent class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
observe_parent: bool = True

When True, the parent token of the position about to be sampled is added to the controller input, as a one-hot vector or as an embedding when use_embedding is set. At least one of the four observation channels must be enabled.

docs.title: observe_sibling class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
observe_sibling: bool = True

When True, the left sibling token of the position about to be sampled is added to the controller input, as a one-hot vector or as an embedding when use_embedding is set. At least one of the four observation channels must be enabled.

docs.title: pinn class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
pinn: PINNConfig | None = None

Settings for the optional PINN surrogate, which alternates symbolic search with training a network on the data and takes derivatives from that trained network. None (the default) searches on finite-difference derivatives. kd.Model takes a PINNConfig or a JSON object of its fields; the network is retrained after generation n_iterations and then every PINNConfig.cycle_n_iterations generations.

docs.title: repeat_max class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
repeat_max: int = 5

Maximum combined number of times the repeat_tokens may appear in one expression; on reaching the count those tokens are removed from the sampling distribution for the rest of that expression. Read only when use_repeat_prior is true.

docs.title: repeat_tokens class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
repeat_tokens: list[str]

Token names counted by the repeat limit, sharing one budget: their occurrences are pooled and compared against repeat_max. Read only when use_repeat_prior is true, and every name must exist in the token library.

docs.title: reward_alpha class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
reward_alpha: float = 0.01

Weight of the complexity penalty in the reward (1 - reward_alpha * complexity) / (1 + sqrt(nmse)). Larger values push the search toward shorter equations; since the reward is clipped at 0, a large value flattens long candidates to zero reward.

docs.title: seed class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
seed: int = 0

Random seed of the search: torch.manual_seed is called with this value when the algorithm is constructed and again before the engine is built, so it governs both the controller's weight initialization and every token sampled from it. It is the only seeding entry and overrides a torch.manual_seed the caller made beforehand.

docs.title: soft_length_loc class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
soft_length_loc: float | None = None

Target expression length in tokens: past position soft_length_loc the sampling logits of operator tokens are reduced by (t - soft_length_loc)**2 / (2 * soft_length_scale), so sampling tends to terminate near that length. None, the default, leaves the prior off.

docs.title: soft_length_scale class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
soft_length_scale: float = 5.0

Width of the length penalty past soft_length_loc, which is (t - soft_length_loc)**2 / (2 * soft_length_scale): larger values make the pull toward the target length gentler. Must be positive, and is read only when soft_length_loc is set.

docs.title: stability_queue_capacity class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
stability_queue_capacity: int = 10

With pinn set and stability_selection greater than 0, the maximum number of distinct candidates kept in the reward-ordered per-cycle pool that stability selection draws from; without pinn, the pool is not read and kd.Model warns on a non-default value. It must be at least as large as stability_selection.

docs.title: stability_selection class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
stability_selection: int = 0

With pinn set, the number of distinct top-reward candidates from the final search cycle that enter bootstrap stability selection, which re-fits each candidate on resampled rows and keeps the one that wins the most resamples; without pinn, no selection runs and kd.Model warns on a non-default value. 0 (the default) skips the step and keeps the best-reward candidate.

docs.title: target_lhs_order class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
target_lhs_order: int

Time-derivative target order, matching dataset.lhs_order.

docs.title: token_bias_tokens class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
token_bias_tokens: tuple[str, ...] = ()

Token names whose sampling probability is shifted by token_bias_weight, identically at every step of every sampled expression. The bias applies only when this list is non-empty and token_bias_weight is not 0.0; a name absent from the token library is skipped.

docs.title: token_bias_weight class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
token_bias_weight: float = 0.0

Amount added to the log-probability of every token in token_bias_tokens, the same at each sampling step. Positive values make those tokens more likely and negative values less likely; 0.0 (the default) leaves the bias off.

docs.title: use_diff_child_prior class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
use_diff_child_prior: bool = True

If True, restrict the child of a derivative token to a state variable or another derivative token; coordinate variables and every other operator are forbidden in that position. This keeps constant terms such as diff_x(x) out of the search.

docs.title: use_diff_descendant_prior class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
use_diff_descendant_prior: bool = True

If True, forbid add and sub anywhere inside the subtree of a derivative token, so no sampled candidate differentiates a sum.

docs.title: use_embedding class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
use_embedding: bool = False

When True, the categorical observation channels enter the controller as learned embeddings of width embedding_dim instead of one-hot vectors. The dangling- slot count is unaffected and stays a single numeric input.

docs.title: use_inverse_prior class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
use_inverse_prior: bool = True

If True, forbid a unary token from being the direct child of its own inverse, so cancelling pairs such as exp(log(u)) and sqrt(n2(u)) are never sampled. Only pairs whose two tokens are both in the library are constrained.

docs.title: use_repeat_prior class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
use_repeat_prior: bool = True

If True, stop a token from being sampled again once it has already appeared repeat_max times in the expression being built. The tokens subject to the limit are named in repeat_tokens; with the defaults this caps add at five and so bounds the number of additive terms.

docs.title: use_trig_prior class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
use_trig_prior: bool = True

If True, forbid trigonometric and derivative tokens anywhere inside the subtree of another trigonometric or derivative token. This rules out compositions such as sin(cos(u)) and, because derivative tokens are included, nested derivatives such as diff_x(diff_x(u)).

docs.title: burgers_preset classmethod
docs.text:
burgers_preset(**overrides: Any) -> DiscoverConfig

Config matching DISCOVER reference for the Burgers equation.

docs.title: chafee_preset classmethod
docs.text:
chafee_preset(**overrides: Any) -> DiscoverConfig

Config matching DISCOVER reference for the Chafee-Infante equation.

docs.title: EqGPTConfig dataclass
docs.text: Static configuration for the EqGPT plugin.

docs.title: asset_dir class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
asset_dir: Path | None = None

Directory holding the pretrained GPT checkpoint at gpt_model/PDEGPT_wave_breaking.pt, consulted when weights_path is unset. With both unset the directory is read from the KD_EQGPT_ASSET_DIR environment variable, and with that unset too the checkpoint is downloaded once from the KD Hub mirror (kd.data.remote.fetch_eqgpt_weights) into the Hugging Face cache.

docs.title: case_filter class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
case_filter: str | None = None

Wave_multicase only: substring matched against the wave-breaking case names: every case whose name contains it is scored, and a candidate's reward is the mean over the cases that could be scored. Setting it selects multi-case wave mode; None (default) keeps the single-case path.

docs.title: coeff_points_per_window class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
coeff_points_per_window: int = 100

Wave_multicase only: number of x sample points per camera window on the grid used for the final coefficient fits. This grid stays separate from the reward grid (reward_points_per_window): scoring runs on the reward grid, the reported coefficients are fitted on this one.

docs.title: exploration_rate class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
exploration_rate: float = 0.2

Probability of drawing the next token uniformly from the legal tokens instead of from the model's distribution, from 0 to 1. The draw is made independently at every token position.

docs.title: finetune_lr class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
finetune_lr: float = 1e-05

Learning rate of the Adam optimizer that fine-tunes the model on the pool of best candidates. A resumed run adopts the current value: the restored optimizer keeps its moment estimates but takes its learning rate from this field.

docs.title: finetune_steps class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
finetune_steps: int = 5

Number of gradient steps taken on the pool of best candidates after each iteration. Each step is one full pass over the pool, and the reported fine-tuning loss is the mean over the steps.

docs.title: is_steady property
docs.text:
is_steady: bool

True when the plugin runs its homogeneous free-pivot path.

docs.title: is_wave_multicase property
docs.text:
is_wave_multicase: bool

True when the plugin runs in multi-case wave mode.

docs.title: masked_tokens class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
masked_tokens: frozenset[int]

Extra vocabulary token ids the sampler must never emit. They are added to the masks the algorithm derives on its own from the declared axes, the derivative order the data supports, and the tokens the platform can represent, so this parameter only ever widens the mask.

docs.title: max_length class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
max_length: int = 49

Maximum number of tokens in a sampled sentence, counting the pinned start_words prefix; it must stay below the model's context length, and the default 49 is the largest value the pretrained model accepts. Sampling stops there if no end token is drawn first, and the value must exceed len(start_words).

docs.title: primary_case class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
primary_case: str | None = None

Wave_multicase only: name of the case, among those case_filter selects, whose coefficient fit is reported as the run's final result. When None (default) the first selected case in sorted order is used; a name outside the selection, or a value given without case_filter, is rejected. The dataset passed to fit must equal this case's data: axis order, field names and every coordinate and field value are compared; the name may differ.

docs.title: reward_points_per_window class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
reward_points_per_window: int = 50

Wave_multicase only: number of x sample points per camera window on the grid used to score candidates. The grid covers three camera windows, so each time slice contributes three times this value; it must be a positive integer.

docs.title: samples_per_epoch class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
samples_per_epoch: int = 400

Number of candidate sentences drawn from the model per iteration; the platform uses it as the batch size for each search iteration. Sentences that cannot be converted into a valid expression are dropped, so fewer candidates may reach scoring.

docs.title: seed class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
seed: int = 0

Random seed of candidate sampling: it seeds the generator that hands every sampling call its own sub-seed, exploration draws included. A run resumed from a checkpoint restores the saved generator state instead, and falls back to this value when the checkpoint carries none. A run resumed with reseed=True branches: it keeps the checkpoint's search state but re-derives the generator from this value, so the branch draws the stream a fresh run on this seed would draw, from the checkpoint's fine-tuned model and elite pool rather than a cold one.

docs.title: sparsity_alpha instance-attribute
docs.text:
sparsity_alpha: float

Weight of the term-count penalty in the reward: a candidate's R^2 is multiplied by 1 - sparsity_alpha * log10(number of distinct terms). It has no default because the value is problem-specific; the Burgers and wave presets pin 0.02 and the steady presets 1.0.

docs.title: start_words class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
start_words: tuple[str, ...] = ('S', 'ut', '+')

Vocabulary words pinned at the head of every sampled sentence, so generation always continues from the same prefix. The default ("S", "ut", "+") fixes the left-hand side to the time derivative, and the prefix is removed from the right- hand side the algorithm reports.

docs.title: steady class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
steady: bool = False

Run the time-independent EqGPT search, where each candidate is a homogeneous relation whose terms sum to zero rather than an equation with a fixed left-hand side. The first term's coefficient is pinned to 1 and the remaining coefficients are fitted by least squares on a surrogate network the algorithm trains itself; enabling it requires start_words=("S",) and steady_activation, and excludes case_filter.

docs.title: steady_activation class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
steady_activation: Literal['sin', 'rational'] | None = None

Activation function of the surrogate network trained in steady mode, either "sin" or "rational". The choice also selects that network's weight initialization; it is required when steady is True and must stay None otherwise.

docs.title: steady_boundary_delete_num class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
steady_boundary_delete_num: int | None = None

Width, in grid cells, of the border removed from the steady evaluation domain; None (the default) keeps every dataset point. A point survives only if it sits at least this many cells from every edge with a fully populated surrounding block, so the data must lie on a grid; it requires steady=True and excludes steady_polar_eval.

docs.title: steady_boundary_grid class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
steady_boundary_grid: tuple[float, ...] | None = None

Grid used only for boundary deletion, given as six numbers in the order (x_start, x_stop, x_step, y_start, y_stop, y_step). Each axis is built with np.arange(start, stop + step, step). When None (the default), the grid uses the distinct coordinate values in the data, so a grid row or column with no data point is missing from it. The eitech and smile presets set this field; it requires steady_boundary_delete_num.

docs.title: steady_constant_column class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
steady_constant_column: bool = False

Add a constant column to the term matrix used to score and refit steady candidates, letting the recovered relation carry a constant offset. Requires steady=True.

docs.title: steady_polar_eval class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
steady_polar_eval: bool = False

Score steady candidates on a generated polar domain instead of the dataset's own points. The domain is 100 radii from 0.5 to 1.45 crossed with 100 angles over the full circle, converted to (x, y); it requires steady=True and excludes steady_boundary_delete_num.

docs.title: steady_surrogate_seed class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
steady_surrogate_seed: int = 525

Random seed for the steady surrogate; it fixes both the network's initial weights and the split of the data into training and validation points. It is separate from seed, which drives candidate sampling, and a value other than the default 525 requires steady=True.

docs.title: steady_train_iters class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
steady_train_iters: int = 50000

Number of optimizer iterations used to train the steady surrogate over the full training sample, 50000 by default. The whole budget runs unless the loss becomes non-finite, in which case training rolls back to the last finite weights and stops; a value other than the default requires steady=True.

docs.title: steady_train_points class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
steady_train_points: int = 10000

Number of dataset points sampled to train the steady surrogate network, 10000 by default. The sample is capped at one below the number of available points so a validation point remains; a value other than the default requires steady=True.

docs.title: steady_validate_points class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
steady_validate_points: int = 1000

Number of points held out from the training sample to validate the steady surrogate, 1000 by default. Training keeps the checkpoint with the lowest validation loss; the count is capped by whatever points steady_train_points leaves, and a value other than the default requires steady=True.

docs.title: top_k class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
top_k: int = 10

Maximum size of the running pool of best candidates, which is held sorted by reward and deduplicated by reward value. The same pool is the corpus the model is fine-tuned on after every iteration, so this sets both the pool cap and the fine- tuning batch.

docs.title: v1_asset_dir class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
v1_asset_dir: Path | None = None

Directory holding the pretrained per-case surrogate checkpoints used to evaluate candidate terms in multi-case wave mode; one checkpoint is loaded per selected case. When None (default), the directory is taken from the KD_V1_WAVE_ASSETS environment variable, and if neither is set the tree is downloaded once from the KD Hub mirror (kd.data.remote.fetch_wave_surrogate_tree).

docs.title: variables class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
variables: tuple[str, ...] | None = None

Coordinate axis names of the dataset; an explicit value must name exactly the dataset's axes, or the run is refused before the search starts, so this field cannot restrict the search to fewer axes. None (the default) takes the axes from the dataset. Vocabulary tokens naming an axis outside this set are masked out of sampling.

docs.title: wave_pkl_path class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
wave_pkl_path: Path | None = None

Path to the pickle file of wave-breaking cases that case_filter selects from. When None (default), it resolves to data/hf- knowledgediscover/WaveBreaking.pkl under the project root, and a missing file raises FileNotFoundError.

docs.title: weights_path class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
weights_path: Path | None = None

Path to the pretrained GPT checkpoint file, taking precedence over asset_dir and the KD_EQGPT_ASSET_DIR environment variable. When set, the file must exist: a missing path raises FileNotFoundError instead of falling back to the other two sources.

docs.title: burgers_preset classmethod
docs.text:
burgers_preset(**overrides: Any) -> EqGPTConfig

EqGPTConfig for the Burgers equation (sparsity_alpha=0.02).

docs.title: steady_preset classmethod
docs.text:
steady_preset(
    dataset: Literal["eitech", "smile", "disk"],
    **overrides: Any,
) -> EqGPTConfig

Build one of the three published steady EqGPT configurations.

docs.title: wave_preset classmethod
docs.text:
wave_preset(**overrides: Any) -> EqGPTConfig

EqGPTConfig for the wave-breaking multi-case showcase.

docs.title: Llm4edConfig dataclass
docs.text: Static configuration for the LLM4ED plugin.

docs.title: base_url class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
base_url: str | None = None

Endpoint URL required by the default provider unless a provider is injected.

docs.title: config property
docs.text:
config: dict[str, Any]

JSON-safe config dict prefixed {"algorithm": "llm4ed", ...}.

docs.title: edge_trim class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
edge_trim: int = 0

Grid cells dropped at each end of every axis (space and time) from the regression rows after the finite differences, so no scored row uses a one-sided boundary stencil. 0 (default) keeps every row, as EDL does (its loaders crop some datasets before differencing instead). Default mode only; it changes the columns every candidate is scored on. The residuals then cover the interior rows only, so the report's residual panels fall back from heatmaps to line plots (with a warning).

docs.title: extra_body class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
extra_body: dict[str, Any] | None = None

Optional request body options forwarded unchanged to the default provider. None omits the SDK keyword; unused when a provider is injected.

docs.title: fit_stop_threshold class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
fit_stop_threshold: float | None

Optional threshold in (0, 1] for the best sparse-reward candidate's unrounded 1 / (1 + NRMSE). None (default) disables fit stopping. NRMSE is RMSE divided by the target's population standard deviation on the native scoring rows, after edge trimming and sketch pin subtraction when applicable. Candidate ranking and the sparse reward stay unchanged. Either this threshold or stop_threshold can stop the run, inclusively, after a completed round. The record uses algorithm_done; an INFO log names the fit threshold and measured fit when this criterion fires. Set via Model(algorithm="llm4ed", fit_stop_threshold=0.995) or this config. It may change on resume; the carried best candidate is re-evaluated on the native scoring rows. This is an in-sample fit criterion.

docs.title: functions class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
functions: tuple[str, ...] = ()

Unary functions the tabular mode offers the LLM and parses (sin, cos, exp, log, sqrt), evaluated without protection: a candidate with a non-finite column is dropped. The default PDE mode refuses a non-empty value.

docs.title: init_num class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
init_num: int = 20

The number of equations the init PROMPT asks the LLM to generate (EDL optimzier_utils.py:108, prompt-text only). Does NOT change the returned batch size, which is n like every round (EDL GENERATION_NUM = args.N covers initialization). Default 20.

docs.title: l0_penalty class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
l0_penalty: float = DEFAULT_L0_PENALTY

STRidge's selection penalty per nonzero term, added to the in-sample MSE. Default 1e-5, EDL's sparse_calculate value.

docs.title: l0_relative class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
l0_relative: bool = False

Multiply l0_penalty by the population variance of the target, so the penalty scales with the data. False (default) is EDL's absolute penalty, which outweighs a real term when var(u_t) is near 1e-5.

docs.title: max_derivative_order class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
max_derivative_order: int = EDL_MAX_ORDER

Highest spatial derivative in the operand vocabulary: 3 (default, EDL's u_x, u_xx, u_xxx) or 4, which adds u_xxxx (and u_yyyy on two axes), computed as Diff2(Diff2(u)), to the columns, the prompts and the parser. Default mode only, and not with a sketch: kd's platform finite differences stop at third order, so the sketch's exit check, and finite-difference refits and consensus verification, cannot evaluate a u_xxxx answer.

docs.title: max_llm_calls_per_propose class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
max_llm_calls_per_propose: int = 50

Plugin-owned upper bound on resample complete() calls within one propose. kd guardrail.

docs.title: max_llm_calls_per_run class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
max_llm_calls_per_run: int = 200

Whole-run call budget fed to the default chain's BudgetedProvider. kd guardrail.

docs.title: max_tokens class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
max_tokens: int = 1024

LLM max decode tokens. Default 1024 (kd-side pin; EDL does not fix a value).

docs.title: model class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
model: str = 'gpt-4o-mini'

LLM model id for the default OpenAICompatProvider (transport; unused when a provider is injected).

docs.title: pool_size class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
pool_size: int = 5

Elite pool capacity k (EDL PriorityQueue). Default 5.

docs.title: reward_limit class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
reward_limit: float = 0.5

filter_score drops candidates with score <= reward_limit. Default 0.5 (EDL).

docs.title: samples_per_epoch class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
samples_per_epoch: int = 8

Per-round proposal count -- the Runner's per-iteration batch size (EDL --N / GENERATION_NUM; the reference script uses 8). Default 8. Read by the plugin's runner_batch_size property.

docs.title: seed class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
seed: int = 0

Base seed for the monotonic per-call LLM seed counter.

docs.title: stop_threshold class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
stop_threshold: float = 0.995

is_done fires when best_reward >= stop_threshold. Default 0.995 (EDL). Sparse reward includes a per-term penalty: a nonempty exact fit scores at most 0.99. Use fit_stop_threshold to stop on fit alone.

docs.title: tape_record_path class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
tape_record_path: str | None = None

Optional JSONL path. When set (and no provider is injected), the default chain wraps the transport in a TapeRecordingProvider so every real request/response is recorded to this path -- the offline replay fixture for CI + the manual real-backend recovery step. None records nothing.

docs.title: temperature class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
temperature: float = 0.8

LLM sampling temperature. Default 0.8 (EDL Burgers, NOT the generic 1.0). Packed into LLMParams per call.

docs.title: PySRConfig dataclass
docs.text:
Frozen configuration for a PySR symbolic-regression run.

Fields: - terms: the Theta library -- the candidate term columns (kd funcall IR) PySR regresses over. Must be non-empty. - seed: random seed forwarded to PySR's random_state. Weak reproducibility only: PySR upstream warns that random_state without deterministic=True and serial execution does not pin run-to-run results (observed in smoke), so under kd defaults the seed makes runs statistically similar, not bit-identical -- and the run manifest's seed inherits this weaker meaning for PySR runs. For full determinism pass extra_pysr_kwargs={"deterministic": True, "parallelism": "serial"}, at a significant speed cost. - niterations: number of PySR internal GP iterations (algebraic generations inside PySR); the facade generations parameter maps here. It controls only PySR's own evolutionary loop, never the kd runner loop. On a resume it is the number of FURTHER iterations the new segment runs from the archived populations (an increment, not a total). - population_size / populations / maxsize: PySR GP knobs (per-population members, number of populations, max expression size). - binary_operators / unary_operators: operator sets exposed to PySR. PDE defaults omit unary operators to avoid fitted constants nested inside structural terms; tabular defaults retain sin/cos/exp/log. Explicit operator sets are preserved. Adding "^" or a custom operator may cause the downstream from_sympy conversion to fail hard. The names are PySR's (symbols, Julia function names, or a Julia definition); kd's funcall names add, mul, n2, n3 and recip are refused with the PySR spelling to use. - extra_pysr_kwargs: a pass-through seam splatted into the underlying PySRRegressor constructor. The caller owns the JSON-safe (and PySR-valid) responsibility for whatever it puts here; defaults to None (never a shared mutable {}). A timeout_in_seconds here is the upper bound of every fit's time limit, re-applied to each segment: a wall-clock deadline announced to the plugin can shorten a fit below it, never lengthen it.

docs.title: binary_operators class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
binary_operators: tuple[str, ...] = ('+', '-', '*', '/')

Binary operators allowed in the PySR expression grammar.

docs.title: extra_pysr_kwargs class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
extra_pysr_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None

Additional PySR backend options; typed configuration keys are refused.

docs.title: target_lhs_order class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
target_lhs_order: int

Order of the PDE left-hand derivative: 1 for u_t, 2 for u_tt.

docs.title: terms class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
terms: tuple[str, ...] = ("u", "u_x", "u_xx", "mul(u, u_x)")

Ordered catalog of candidate columns for PDE regression. On a grid whose spatial axes are x and y, kd.Model builds the default over both axes, u, u_x, u_xx, mul(u, u_x), u_y, u_yy, mul(u, u_y).

docs.title: unary_operators class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
unary_operators: tuple[str, ...] = ()

Unary operators allowed in the PySR expression grammar.

docs.title: PySINDyConfig dataclass
docs.text: Frozen configuration for a PySINDy STLSQ fit.

docs.title: alpha class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
alpha: float

Weight of the ridge (L2) penalty in every least-squares solve of the sequentially thresholded fit, so it changes which coefficients fall below threshold; must be finite and at least 0, and 0 makes each solve ordinary least squares. The default is PySINDy STLSQ's own. The penalty acts on the columns as the solve sees them: with normalize_columns on, every column has unit norm, so the same value weighs more against each coefficient than on raw columns of large norm. unbias refits the selected terms without it.

docs.title: degree class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
degree: int = 2

Highest total degree of the polynomial library, used only on tabular data; must be at least 1. The library holds the constant term one listed first, followed by every monomial of the feature columns of degree 1 through degree.

docs.title: extra_optimizer_kwargs class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
extra_optimizer_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None

Extra keyword arguments forwarded to the underlying PySINDy optimizer for settings with no field of their own, such as ridge_kw. threshold, max_iter, normalize_columns, unbias and alpha are rejected here, because a shadowed value would leave the recorded configuration describing a fit that never ran. Set those fields directly instead.

docs.title: max_iter class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
max_iter: int = 20

Upper bound on the number of thresholding rounds the fit runs, in iterations; must be greater than 0. It caps the solver's own convergence loop rather than a search budget, so kd.Model(generations=...) leaves it unchanged and it can only be set here.

docs.title: normalize_columns class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
normalize_columns: bool = False

Whether the fit rescales the library columns to comparable magnitude before thresholding, so a term's units alone do not decide whether it survives. Turning it on moves the scale that threshold acts on, so the two are chosen together; reported coefficients are returned in the original units either way. relative_threshold requires it to be on.

docs.title: relative_threshold class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
relative_threshold: bool = False

Whether threshold is read as a fraction of the regression target's L2 norm instead of an absolute coefficient magnitude. A term then survives a thresholding round when its coefficient times its column norm reaches threshold times the target norm, so rescaling a column or the target leaves the selected terms unchanged. Requires normalize_columns=True. With anchored terms, the norm is that of the target left after the anchored columns are projected out.

docs.title: seed class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
seed: int = 0

Random seed recorded in the run manifest next to the dataset fingerprint. This fit is deterministic and never draws on the value, so changing it alone does not change the result.

docs.title: target_lhs_order class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
target_lhs_order: int

Order of the PDE left-hand derivative: 1 for u_t, 2 for u_tt.

docs.title: terms class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
terms: tuple[str, ...] = ("u", "u_x", "u_xx", "mul(u, u_x)")

Ordered catalog of candidate right-hand-side terms; each entry becomes one column of the regression matrix, in the order given. The catalog must be non-empty and its entries must stay distinct once canonicalized; the fit reports the terms whose coefficients survive thresholding. On a grid whose spatial axes are x and y, kd.Model builds the default over both axes, u, u_x, u_xx, mul(u, u_x), u_y, u_yy, mul(u, u_y).

docs.title: threshold class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
threshold: float = 0.1

Coefficient magnitude below which a candidate term is dropped during the sequentially thresholded fit; must be finite and at least 0. A value too large for the data leaves nothing selected, which raises an error quoting the current threshold instead of returning an empty equation. With relative_threshold on, it is instead a dimensionless fraction of the target's L2 norm.

docs.title: unbias class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
unbias: bool = True

Whether the fit ends with an unregularized least-squares refit over the terms that survived thresholding, undoing the shrinkage the sparse fit introduces. The result reports the coefficients from that final refit, so this setting is visible in the published coefficient values.

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
KD fits two kinds of dataset. Field data is a kd.PDEDataset: fields sampled on coordinate axes, either on a regular grid or at scattered points. A regression table is a kd.TabularDataset: a feature matrix X, a target y and their names. Model.fit accepts either. ODE trajectories are held in a kd.data.TrajectorySet, which is not a fit input; it is converted to one table per target state, as described under ODE trajectories.

Three constructors build a PDEDataset from data you already hold: from_arrays for fields on a regular grid, from_scatter for points that are not on one, and from_xlsx for a workbook whose columns are already coordinates and values. kd.load reads a catalog id or a file into a PDEDataset, a TrajectorySet or a TabularDataset, chosen by kind= or by the mappings given (see Data requirements); kd.inspect_file lists the arrays of a file beforehand and names the registered layouts that recognize it in SourceReport.layouts. kd.load_tabular reads a table file into a TabularDataset. On a grid dataset, with_field returns a copy with one field replaced and window a copy restricted to a coordinate range on one axis. The constructors and both methods are documented under the class below.

A field dataset states three things before a search can start: which fields it carries, which axes they are sampled on, and which term is the left-hand side. The requirements for each are described under Data requirements, and the datasets shipped with the package are listed under Dataset catalog.

Name Summary kd.PDEDataset(name, task_type[, ...]) Complete PDE dataset specification. kd.load(source, kind[, ...]) Load a catalog dataset, grid data, ODE trajectories or a regression table. kd.load_tabular(path, name) Load float64 columns, validating names and shapes through the tabular bridge. kd.inspect_file(path) Describe arrays in a file before choosing a dataset layout or mapping. kd.compute_dataset_fingerprint(dataset) Return the content fingerprint of a grid dataset, trajectory set or table. kd.TabularDataset(X, y[, ...]) A scalar regression dataset: features X, target y, docs.title: PDEDataset dataclass
docs.text:
Complete PDE dataset specification.

Attributes:

  • name (str) –

    Dataset identifier

  • task_type (TaskType) –

    Type of problem (PDE, ODE, regression)

  • topology (DataTopology) –

    Data layout (grid, scattered, or tabular)

  • axes (dict[str, AxisInfo] | None) –

    Mapping from axis name to AxisInfo. GRID: each AxisInfo.values is that axis's coordinate vector (length = grid dimension size).

  • axis_order (list[str] | None) –

    Ordered list of axis names defining tensor dimensions

  • fields (dict[str, FieldData] | None) –

    Mapping from field name to FieldData. GRID: nD tensor shaped by axis_order. SCATTERED: 1-D per-point vector (length N). TABULAR: same-length 1-D feature and target columns.

  • lhs_field (str) –

    Field for LHS of equation (e.g., "u")

  • lhs_axis (str) –

    Axis for time derivative on LHS (e.g., "t" for u_t = RHS)

  • lhs_order (int) –

    Order of the LHS derivative along lhs_axis (0 -> homogeneous / no evolution LHS with empty lhs_axis + lhs_field, 1 -> u_t, 2 -> u_tt for the wave/telegraph case). Default 1.

  • noise_level (float) –

    Amount of noise added to data

  • ground_truth (str | None) –

    Optional ground truth equation string

  • source (DatasetSource | None) –

    Provenance recorded by kd.load for a file-loaded dataset (path, sha256, container, layout, hints, sample selection); None otherwise. Not hashed into the fingerprint.

Example

dataset = PDEDataset( ... name="burgers", ... task_type=TaskType.PDE, ... axes={"x": x_axis, "t": t_axis}, ... axis_order=["x", "t"], ... fields={"u": u_field}, ... lhs_field="u", ... lhs_axis="t", ... )

docs.text:
from_arrays(
    coords: dict[str, Tensor | ndarray | Sequence[float]],
    fields: dict[str, Tensor | ndarray],
    *,
    lhs: str | None = "u_t",
    periodic: Iterable[str] | None = None,
    name: str = "custom",
    ground_truth: str | None = None,
    dtype: dtype = float64,
) -> PDEDataset

Factory: wrap raw arrays into a PDEDataset.

Parameters:

  • coords (dict[str, Tensor | ndarray | Sequence[float]]) –

    Mapping axis name to 1D coordinate tensor (or numpy/list). Insertion order defines axis_order.

  • fields (dict[str, Tensor | ndarray]) –

    Mapping field name to nD field tensor whose shape matches (len(coords[axis_0]), len(coords[axis_1]), ...).

  • lhs (str | None, default: 'u_t' ) –

    Combined LHS spec "{field}_{axis...}" encoding the LHS derivative via the kd naming convention. "u_t" -> field "u", axis "t", order 1 (du/dt); "u_tt" -> order 2 (the wave/telegraph LHS d²u/dt²).

  • periodic (Iterable[str] | None, default: None ) –

    Iterable of axis names that are periodic.

  • name (str, default: 'custom' ) –

    Dataset identifier (printed in repr).

  • ground_truth (str | None, default: None ) –

    Optional ground-truth equation string.

  • dtype (dtype, default: float64 ) –

    Float dtype to cast coords + fields to (default float64).

Returns:

  • PDEDataset –

    A validated PDEDataset.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If lhs spec is malformed, references a missing field/axis, or field shapes don't match coords.

Example

ds = PDEDataset.from_arrays( ... coords={"x": x_array, "t": t_array}, ... fields={"u": u_array}, # shape (len(x), len(t)) ... lhs="u_t", ... periodic={"x"}, ... )

from_scatter(
    coords: dict[str, Tensor | ndarray | Sequence[float]],
    fields: dict[str, Tensor | ndarray],
    *,
    lhs: str | None = "u_t",
    name: str = "custom",
    ground_truth: str | None = None,
    dtype: dtype = float64,
    allow_nan: bool = False,
) -> PDEDataset

Factory: wrap raw per-point scatter arrays into a SCATTERED dataset.

Parameters:

  • coords (dict[str, Tensor | ndarray | Sequence[float]]) –

    Mapping axis name to a 1-D per-point coordinate array (or numpy/list). Insertion order defines axis_order.

  • fields (dict[str, Tensor | ndarray]) –

    Mapping field name to a 1-D per-point value array of the same length N as the coords.

  • lhs (str | None, default: 'u_t' ) –

    LHS spec. "u_t" (default) parses via the kd naming convention to (field, axis, order) for the evolution / wave track (pivot pinned to u_t).

  • name (str, default: 'custom' ) –

    Dataset identifier.

  • ground_truth (str | None, default: None ) –

    Optional ground-truth equation string.

  • dtype (dtype, default: float64 ) –

    Float dtype to cast coords + fields to (default float64).

  • allow_nan (bool, default: False ) –

    Whether to retain NaN values in the axes/fields. Intended for a missing-value-preserving ingress such as from_xlsx with drop_na=False; default False keeps ordinary scatter construction finite-only.

Returns:

  • PDEDataset –

    A validated SCATTERED PDEDataset.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If coords/fields is empty, a coord/field is not 1-D, the coords + fields do not share one length N, or the (non-empty) lhs spec references a missing field/axis.

docs.title: FieldReport dataclass
docs.text:
Per-field facts of one dataset field.

Attributes:

  • name (str) –

    Field name as it appears in dataset.fields.

  • dtype (str) –

    Torch dtype without the torch. prefix (e.g. "float64").

  • shape (tuple[int, ...]) –

    Tensor shape as a tuple of ints.

  • min (float) –

    Smallest value over the FINITE entries; NaN when nothing is finite.

  • max (float) –

    Largest value over the finite entries; NaN when nothing is finite.

  • mean (float) –

    Mean over the finite entries; NaN when nothing is finite.

  • nan_count (int) –

    Number of NaN entries.

  • inf_count (int) –

    Number of Inf entries (either sign).

  • noise_estimate (dict[str, float]) –

    Robust relative noise level along each axis: the median absolute deviation (MAD) of the second difference u[i-1] - 2*u[i] + u[i+1], scaled by 1.4826 / sqrt(6) and divided by the field's population standard deviation.

  • first_derivative_gap (dict[str, float]) –

    Relative gap ||2C - E|| / ||E|| between the second-order central first differences C = u[i+1] - u[i-1] (step 1) and E = u[i+2] - u[i-2] (step 2).

  • second_derivative_gap (dict[str, float]) –

    Relative gap ||4A - B|| / ||B|| between the second-order central second differences A = u[i-1] - 2*u[i] + u[i+1] (step 1) and B = u[i-2] - 2*u[i] + u[i+2] (step 2).

  • constant_axes (list[str] | None) –

    Grid axes along which every observed slice is exactly equal, in axis order. Only axes with at least two samples qualify. None means unmeasured (non-grid, no axes, or non-finite field).

  • noise_limited_axes (list[str] | None) –

    Eligible grid axes whose pooled von Neumann ratio is within three standard deviations of independent Gaussian white noise (mean 2). Measures unresolved ordered variation, not a physical role.

Here u[i] is the field value at index i (0-based) along the axis, out of n points. Both gaps use the common interior 2 <= i <= n-3. The MAD, the standard deviation and both L2 norms pool all other dimensions of the field. The grid spacing cancels from both ratios. A gap is 0 when step 1 and step 2 give the same derivative and grows as the two results diverge (noise or unresolved structure along the axis). The gaps describe the raw field, not the derivative method a fit uses. All three diagnostics are computed on uniformly spaced axes with at least five points, and only for a field without NaN or Inf values.

The three diagnostic dicts share eligible axis keys in axis_order order; an absent key means the axis was not eligible. In these dicts a serialized null means the computed value is infinite, while null in min, max or mean means no finite value exists.

docs.title: derivative_field
docs.text:
derivative_field(
    dataset: PDEDataset,
    field: str,
    axis: str,
    order: int = 1,
    *,
    derivatives: str = "finite_diff",
) -> Tensor

Return the order-th derivative of field along axis on the grid.

Parameters:

  • dataset (PDEDataset) –

    A GRID dataset.

  • field (str) –

    Name of the field to differentiate.

  • axis (str) –

    Name of the axis to differentiate along.

  • order (int, default: 1 ) –

    Derivative order, 1 to 3.

  • derivatives (str, default: 'finite_diff' ) –

    "finite_diff" or "fd2".

Raises:

  • KeyError –

    if derivatives is not a registered provider, or field or axis is not in the dataset.

  • ValueError –

    if the provider differentiates a trained field network ("autograd") or was registered by an extension, the dataset is not a GRID dataset, order is outside 1 to 3, an axis is not evenly spaced or has fewer than five points, or a field holds NaN or Inf.

Example

import kd dataset = kd.load_burgers() u_t = kd.derivative_field(dataset, "u", "t") smoothed = kd.lowpass_smooth(dataset, modes=32) u_t_smoothed = kd.derivative_field(smoothed, "u", "t") u_t.shape == dataset.get_field("u").shape True

docs.title: NetworkSmoothingQuality dataclass
docs.text:
Answer-blind diagnostics of one network smoothing.

Attributes:

  • requested_epochs (int) –

    The recipe's epoch budget.

  • executed_epochs (int) –

    Epochs the fit ran (TrainingResult.epochs_run).

  • stopping_reason (Literal['max_epochs', 'early_stopped']) –

    "early_stopped" when patience ended the fit, "max_epochs" when it ran the budget.

  • final_train_loss (float) –

    Training loss of the last epoch.

  • best_val_loss (float | None) –

    Lowest validation loss, None without a validation split.

  • loss_scale (float) –

    Population variance of the observed field, the loss of predicting its mean everywhere. Both losses are mean squared errors in field units squared, so a loss divided by this scale is a relative squared error.

  • sigma_hat (dict[str, float | None]) –

    Per field, the second-difference MAD noise estimate (kd.data.diagnostics.noise_estimate) converted to field units, the smallest over the axes with at least MIN_STENCIL_POINTS points; None without such an axis.

  • residual_ratio (dict[str, float | None]) –

    Per field, rms(observed - predicted) / sigma_hat over the whole grid; None when sigma_hat is zero or unavailable.

  • device (str) –

    The device the fit ran on.

  • cuda_max_memory_allocated_bytes (int | None) –

    torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated of that device read after the fit, the process's peak through the fit (the counter is not reset, so other readers keep theirs); None for a fit off CUDA.

  • unavailable (dict[str, str]) –

    Reason per quantity that could not be computed, keyed "<quantity>.<field>" for a per-field quantity and by the bare name otherwise.

docs.title: Dataset catalog
docs.text:
Datasets ship with the package or download on first use, and the catalog is how they are addressed: kd.list_datasets enumerates them, kd.get_dataset takes one stable id, and both return a kd.DatasetSpec carrying the equation, the left-hand side, the axes and the loader itself. Their provenance is tabulated under Bundled datasets. The generate_* functions synthesize data from an analytic solution instead, for self-checks.

The named loaders at the end of this page are the short spelling of a catalog entry, not a second way in: kd.load_kdv is the object kd.get_dataset("kdv") carries as its loader. A few of the bundled datasets have no such name and are reached through the catalog alone.

docs.title: Batch experiments
docs.text:
kd.harness runs a matrix of fits and keeps what it ran. The loop is four calls: an ExperimentPlan of PlanEntry rows states the matrix, run_plan executes it into a fresh directory, EvidenceStore.load reopens that directory and re-verifies it, and build_consensus groups the runs by the law each one selected. merge_stores combines the stores of separate run_plan batches into one store before that last step. The store's guarantees and the meaning of the consensus axes are described under Batch experiments and evidence.

These names are imported from the subpackage rather than the package root: from kd.harness import ExperimentPlan, run_plan. Listed below are the entry points a caller writes; the module also carries the artifact machinery that run_plan and build_consensus drive on their own.

run_episode runs one plan entry and returns its EpisodeOutcome; given run_dir=, it also creates and seals that entry's run directory.

environment_fingerprint returns the runtime fingerprint stored in a new evidence index: the KD, CPython and PyTorch versions, the platform, the git commit and the working-tree status. With strict=True it raises instead of recording a field it cannot read as "unknown".

ProcessSupervisor, run_supervised, ProcessResult and ProcessEnding supervise a single worker command and every process it starts, for a caller that launches its own worker processes. On Linux the command leads its own process group, and a time limit or a stop request sends SIGTERM to the group, then SIGKILL after a grace period. On Windows, which has no signal that asks a process tree to stop, the command runs in a Job Object that is terminated when the grace period ends. Process supervision does not support other platforms yet. The optional memory cap (memory_max_gb) is a systemd user scope on Linux, the command prefix that build_capped_command assembles, and a limit on the committed memory of the Job Object on Windows. check_memory_cap_available checks that the platform's cap can be applied before any work starts.

Name Summary kd.harness.ExperimentPlan(name, entries) An ordered execution matrix of plan entries with a content identity. kd.harness.PlanEntry(instrument, dataset_ref[, ...]) One declarative episode: an instrument applied to a dataset at a seed. kd.harness.run_plan(plan, datasets[, ...]) Pre-flight, then run every plan entry into a fresh store. kd.harness.PlanRunResult(store_root, outcomes) The outcome of a whole batch: the store root plus every episode outcome. kd.harness.run_episode(entry, entry_index[, ...]) Run one plan entry and return a totalized EpisodeOutcome. kd.harness.EpisodeOutcome(entry_index, entry[, ...]) The sealed result of running one plan entry. kd.harness.merge_stores(sources, root[, ...]) Merge sealed stores into a new store at root; return it reloaded. kd.harness.EvidenceStore(root, plan[, ...]) A fresh-dir, append-only, tamper-evident batch evidence directory. kd.harness.build_consensus(store, datasets[, ...]) Aggregate a sealed evidence store into a consensus report tree. kd.harness.ConsensusReport(provenance, datasets[, ...]) The full consensus report tree for one sealed evidence store. kd.harness.render_consensus_markdown(report, store) Render the report as a deterministic Markdown document (pure function). kd.harness.SKETCH_SIDECAR_FILENAME — kd.harness.RESULT_SIDECAR_FILENAME — kd.harness.REPORT_SIDECAR_DIRNAME — kd.harness.EpisodeOutputError(outcome) A requested result.json or report/ failed after the seal. kd.harness.environment_fingerprint(strict) Return the runtime fingerprint stored in a fresh evidence index. kd.harness.ProcessSupervisor(command, env[, ...]) Launch a command and supervise its whole process tree. kd.harness.run_supervised(command, env[, ...]) Launch a process tree and block until cleanup or the final grace bound. kd.harness.ProcessResult(pid, returncode[, ...]) Observed leader termination, group cleanup, timing and sampled memory. kd.harness.ProcessEnding(value, names[, ...]) Escalation stage reached while the leader was observed alive. kd.harness.build_capped_command(command, memory_max_gb) Prefix a command with a systemd user scope enforcing memory and no swap. kd.harness.check_memory_cap_available() Check that this platform's kernel memory cap can be applied to a command.

docs.title: run_plan
docs.text:
run_plan(
    plan: ExperimentPlan,
    *,
    datasets: Mapping[str, PDEDataset | TabularDataset],
    store_root: Path,
    model_factory: Callable[..., Any] = Model,
    device: str | None = None,
    recording: RecordingOptions | None = None,
    catalog_path: Path | None = None,
    parallel: ParallelOptions | None = None,
) -> PlanRunResult

Pre-flight, then run every plan entry into a fresh store.

Parameters:

  • plan (ExperimentPlan) –

    The ordered execution matrix to run.

  • datasets (Mapping[str, PDEDataset | TabularDataset]) –

    Maps each dataset_ref to a loaded PDEDataset or a public TabularDataset (normalized once at entry through the same seam as Model.fit).

  • store_root (Path) –

    Fresh directory for the EvidenceStore (must not exist or must be empty; append/resume is out of scope).

  • model_factory (Callable[..., Any], default: Model ) –

    Facade constructor forwarded to run_episode; injectable so unit tests can stub the fit (serial runs only).

  • device (str | None, default: None ) –

    Execution-environment parameter forwarded to run_episode and, from there, conditionally to the facade. None leaves the serial-execution call form literally unchanged.

  • recording (RecordingOptions | None, default: None ) –

    When set, each entry runs inside a standard run dir <store_root>/runs/entry-NNNN/ (numbered by plan entry, matching records/entry-NNNN.json) wired per the options.

  • catalog_path (Path | None, default: None ) –

    Cross-run ledger to append one kd-runcat-v1 row per outcome (requires recording; rows carry the entry index, the store's plan hash and paths relative to the catalog file).

  • parallel (ParallelOptions | None, default: None ) –

    Run entries in supervised child processes; None runs them serially in this process.

Returns:

  • PlanRunResult –

    A PlanRunResult with the store root and one outcome per entry.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If pre-flight finds any unknown instrument or unresolved dataset_ref (all violations are collected into the message), if catalog_path is given without recording, or, with parallel, if model_factory is not Model, an instrument was registered in this process only (a child process would not have it), an entry device is not None/"cpu"/"cuda", or the card pool cannot serve parallel.limits.
