run_episode(
    *,
    entry: PlanEntry,
    entry_index: int,
    dataset: PDEDataset | TabularDataset,
    model_factory: Callable[..., Any] = Model,
    device: str | None = None,
    run_dir: Path | None = None,
    run_id: str | None = None,
    resume_from: Path | str | None = None,
    reseed: bool = False,
    sketch: Sketch | SketchSpec | None = None,
    verify: VerifyPolicy | None = None,
    max_seconds: float | None = None,
    recording: RecordingOptions | None = None,
    record_ref: str | None = None,
    persist_outcome: Callable[[EpisodeOutcome], None]
    | None = None,
    extra_callbacks: Sequence[RunnerCallback] | None = None,
) -> EpisodeOutcome

Run one plan entry and return a totalized EpisodeOutcome.

Parameters:

  • entry (PlanEntry) –

    The declarative plan entry to execute.

  • entry_index (int) –

    The entry's position in the plan (for logging / storage).

  • dataset (PDEDataset | TabularDataset) –

    The loaded dataset resolved from entry.dataset_ref.

  • model_factory (Callable[..., Any], default: Model ) –

    Facade constructor; injectable so unit tests can stub it.

  • device (str | None, default: None ) –

    Execution-environment knob forwarded to the facade (a sibling of verbose).

  • run_dir (Path | None, default: None ) –

    A FRESH standard run directory (kd.search.run_dir) this episode claims and seals: iteration events, phase lines, a manifest-managed checkpoints/ and the run-level manifest all land there. None disables run-directory recording.

  • run_id (str | None, default: None ) –

    The operational handle of this episode's run dir, for a caller that names the run before it starts (a queue that files its own state under the same id). Requires run_dir and must be non-empty.

  • resume_from (Path | str | None, default: None ) –

    Optional checkpoint path forwarded to model.fit — harness-owned, so retry lanes can resume a prior segment's checkpoint; lineage lands in the record's manifest (M4).

  • reseed (bool, default: False ) –

    Forwarded to model.fit to turn that resume into a BRANCH (K4): the restored search state is kept and the random streams are re-derived from entry.seed. True without resume_from is the facade's ValueError, totalized as a "raised" outcome like any other fit failure.

  • sketch (Sketch | SketchSpec | None, default: None ) –

    Forwarded to model.fit(sketch=...) as given; a shorthand kd.SketchSpec is resolved there, against dataset.

  • verify (VerifyPolicy | None, default: None ) –

    Forwarded to model.fit(verify=...). None lets the facade resolve the sketch exit's own default (kd.SKETCH_EXIT_VERIFY); it is NOT the report-only VerifyPolicy(), which a caller opts into explicitly.

  • max_seconds (float | None, default: None ) –

    Forwarded to model.fit(max_seconds=...): the fit's wall-clock budget, whose clock starts when the facade's fit is called. Like the sketch, it stays out of the plan's identity hash.

  • recording (RecordingOptions | None, default: None ) –

    Knobs for the run-dir surfaces; defaults to RecordingOptions() when run_dir is set.

  • record_ref (str | None, default: None ) –

    Pointer (relative to run_dir) to the sealed record's external home (the store's records/entry-NNNN.json) — the run dir then references instead of duplicating it. Requires run_dir.

  • persist_outcome (Callable[[EpisodeOutcome], None] | None, default: None ) –

    Called with the finished outcome BEFORE the run dir is sealed, so the record record_ref points at is written before the manifest that advertises it.

  • extra_callbacks (Sequence[RunnerCallback] | None, default: None ) –

    Additional RunnerCallback instances forwarded to the facade's callbacks seam. On the recording path they follow the harness-owned IterationEventEmitter.

Returns:

  • EpisodeOutcome –

    An EpisodeOutcome whose status is one of "completed", "raised", or "no_record"; when run_dir is set it also carries the sealed run dir's run_id / run_dir.

docs.title: ProcessResult dataclass
docs.text:
Observed leader termination, group cleanup, timing and sampled memory.

Attributes:

  • pid (int) –

    Leader PID; on Linux also the supervised process group ID.

  • returncode (int | None) –

    Leader exit status, or None if still alive at the bound. On Linux a negative value is the signal that ended it. On Windows it is the unsigned 32-bit exit code, and a leader ended by the Job termination reports 1.

  • ended_by (ProcessEnding) –

    Last escalation stage reached while the leader was alive.

  • stop_reason (Literal['timeout', 'requested'] | None) –

    timeout or requested when either initiated the escalation; None for natural exit and its descendant cleanup.

  • sigkill_used (bool) –

    Whether the group SIGKILL step was taken, including descendant cleanup and an OS refusal of that signal. Always False on Windows.

  • started_at (str) –

    Launch time as a UTC ISO 8601 string.

  • term_sent_at (str | None) –

    UTC time of the SIGTERM step, or None. Always None on Windows.

  • kill_sent_at (str | None) –

    UTC time of the SIGKILL step, or None. Always None on Windows.

  • ended_at (str) –

    UTC time when supervision finished.

  • wallclock_seconds (float) –

    Elapsed monotonic seconds from launch to completion.

  • peak_rss_bytes (int) –

    Maximum sampled sum of group members' resident memory.

  • left_descendants (bool) –

    Whether the leader exited before escalation and left members requiring cleanup.

  • group_emptied (bool) –

    Whether the group was confirmed empty. False means the grace after the SIGKILL or Job termination step expired with members still present.

  • memory_backend (Literal['linux-cgroup', 'windows-job'] | None) –

    Kernel mechanism enforcing the memory cap: linux-cgroup limits resident memory, windows-job limits committed memory. None when no cap was requested.

  • memory_limit_bytes (int | None) –

    The enforced cap in bytes, or None without a cap.

  • peak_committed_bytes (int | None) –

    Windows: the Job's peak committed memory as the kernel reports it, with or without a cap. The kernel counts a request the cap refused, so the value can exceed the cap. None on Linux.

  • job_terminated_at (str | None) –

    UTC time of the Job termination step (Windows), including descendant cleanup, or None.

docs.title: Model and result
docs.text:
kd.Model runs a search and returns a kd.ExperimentResult.

import kd

model = kd.Model(algorithm="sga", generations=200, seed=42)
model.fit(kd.load_kdv())
print(model.result_.equation, model.best_score_)

algorithm takes the name of any of the seven algorithms; each one's scope and parameters are on its own page under Algorithms. Passing config= supplies that algorithm's settings and becomes the single source for them, so supplying the same settings as keywords alongside it raises. Which parameters may change on a resume is covered in Parameter tiers and resuming, and what best_score_ measures in Score conventions and comparability.

After fit, report(output_dir) renders the figures this fit supports and an HTML report into output_dir, as described under Figure generation. fit(sketch=...) takes a partially specified equation built with kd.Sketch: pinned terms with fixed coefficients, anchored terms whose coefficients are fitted, and holes for unknown terms. How far each algorithm mode enforces each clause is declared in its schema; the clauses are described under Complete a partial equation.

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
High-level facade for PDE discovery (PySR-style API).

Parameters:

  • algorithm (str, default: 'sga' ) –

    Search algorithm name.

  • generations (int, default: 50 ) –

    Search-loop length (default 50).

  • population (int, default: 20 ) –

    SGA population size (number of PDE candidates). SGA-only.

  • depth (int, default: 4 ) –

    Maximum tree depth per term. SGA-only.

  • width (int, default: 5 ) –

    Maximum number of terms per PDE. SGA-only.

  • aic_ratio (float, default: 1.0 ) –

    AIC penalty ratio. SGA-only.

  • derivatives (str, default: 'finite_diff' ) –

    Registered provider for a mode declaring platform derivatives; omission preserves that mode's declared default.

  • seed (int, default: 0 ) –

    Random seed for reproducibility. It threads into every algorithm's default config when config= is unset; otherwise the config's own seed wins. Passing the facade seed= together with config= is rejected by _validate_config_exclusivity.

  • verbose (bool, default: True ) –

    When True, print per-iteration progress to stdout.

  • config (object | None, default: None ) –

    Optional pre-built SGAConfig, DLGAConfig, DiscoverConfig, PySRConfig, EqGPTConfig, Llm4edConfig, or PySINDyConfig, or an instance of a registered algorithm's config class. When provided, it is the single source of plugin settings.

  • callbacks (list[RunnerCallback] | None, default: None ) –

    Optional list of additional RunnerCallback instances to attach to the runner. The verbose progress printer is appended automatically when verbose=True.

  • surrogate_model (Module | StoredSurrogate | str | Path | None, default: None ) –

    Optional pre-trained NN_1 forwarded to DLGAPlugin(surrogate_model=...): a torch.nn.Module, injected as given; a kd.models.StoredSurrogate.

  • provider (LLMProvider | None, default: None ) –

    Optional pre-built kd.llm.LLMProvider forwarded to Llm4edPlugin(provider=...). llm4ed-only — passing it with any other algorithm raises TypeError (silent drop is a bug-attractor).

  • checkpoint_dir (str | Path | None, default: None ) –

    Optional directory for periodic checkpoints.

  • checkpoint_every (int, default: 10 ) –

    Save a per-iteration checkpoint every N iterations (0-indexed: saves at 0, N, 2N, ...; default 10).

  • checkpoint_keep_last (int | None, default: None ) –

    Retention bound on PERIODIC checkpoints. None (default) keeps every one, so that the evidence trail stays complete; an int >= 1 keeps only the N most recent periodic checkpoints, pruning older ones from both the manifest and disk.

  • phases_path (str | Path | None, default: None ) –

    Optional phases.jsonl sink (kd-runphase-v1).

  • savgol_window (int, default: 0 ) –

    Savitzky-Golay smoothing window length. 0 (default) disables smoothing. A positive value smooths every field along every grid axis with that window length and polynomial order 3 before the search.

  • small_term_rtol (float, default: 0.0 ) –

    Relative coefficient threshold for the final answer. 0.0 (default) keeps the algorithm's answer. A value r in (0, 1) drops every term whose finite coefficient magnitude is below r times the largest finite coefficient magnitude.

  • **kwargs (Any, default: {} ) –

    Forwarded to the selected algorithm's config dataclass when the field is not already owned by a facade parameter. Unknown, cross-algorithm, colliding, or JSON-type-invalid fields raise at construction.

docs.title: fit
docs.text:
fit(
    dataset: PDEDataset | TabularDataset,
    resume_from: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    sketch: Sketch | SketchSpec | None = None,
    reseed: bool = False,
    verify: VerifyPolicy | None = None,
    max_seconds: float | None = None,
) -> Model

Run the search and populate post-fit attributes.

Parameters:

  • dataset (PDEDataset | TabularDataset) –

    A PDE dataset or public X -> y regression table.

  • resume_from (str | Path | None, default: None ) –

    Optional path to a checkpoint file written by a previous run (checkpoint_*.pt). The checkpoint restores search state (population / controller weights / best).

  • sketch (Sketch | SketchSpec | None, default: None ) –

    Optional semantic search-space contract for this fit, built with kd.Sketch: pinned terms are deducted from the regression target and restored with their exact coefficients, and the run's result carries a sound SketchOutcome (result_.sketch_outcome) whose solution is only filled when the discovered law satisfies every sketch clause AND fits the data within verify (see below).

  • reseed (bool, default: False ) –

    Turn the resume into a BRANCH (K4). A plain resume keeps the checkpoint's random streams and continues one trajectory.

  • verify (VerifyPolicy | None, default: None ) –

    Residual gate the sketch exit judges the lifted law with. None resolves to kd.SKETCH_EXIT_VERIFY (nmse_max=0.05), so a sketch fit certifies only a law that also fits the data on the platform's own footing.

  • max_seconds (float | None, default: None ) –

    Optional wall-clock budget for the whole fit, in seconds, positive and finite.

Returns:

  • Model –

    self for sklearn-style chaining.

Raises:

  • NotImplementedError –

    If algorithm is not supported.

  • TypeError –

    If sketch is not a Sketch, a SketchSpec or None.

  • ValueError –

    If sketch uses a clause the algorithm's capability declaration does not support, is an evolution sketch on a table or an order-0 (table) sketch on evolution data, or declares an LHS differing from the dataset's resolved LHS, or if a SketchSpec does not resolve on the dataset.

  • FileNotFoundError –

    If resume_from does not exist.

  • IsADirectoryError –

    If resume_from points at a directory.

  • RuntimeError –

    If a LEGACY resume_from (no config snapshot) was written by a structurally different config (state_dict shape mismatch on restore); a snapshot-bearing checkpoint hits the ValueError tier gate first.

docs.title: Result structure
docs.text:
One fit produces one ExperimentResult, and the trailing-underscore attributes above are shortcuts into it. Its contents fall into four groups, and the entry below lists every field:

  • The answer. best_expression and best_score, with score_kind and score_direction stating what that number is and which direction is better. A fit with a sketch also fills sketch_outcome, which carries the clause verdict and a certified solution when the selected law satisfies every clause and fits the data.
  • Fit quality. final_eval, an EvaluationResult carrying mse, nmse, r² and the coefficients, alongside the actual and predicted values behind them.
  • Search progress. iterations, early_stopped, and recorder, the per-iteration record that kd.VizEngine draws from.
  • Provenance. dataset_name, algorithm_name and config, plus the manifest and run_record that seal the run against its inputs.

docs.title: Interruption of a running fit
docs.text:
kd.SearchInterrupted is the exception an embedding process raises inside a running fit to stop it: a signal handler, or a watchdog that enforces a wall-clock budget. The search stack lets this exception through instead of recording it as one more invalid candidate, so fit exits with it and the caller decides what to keep. The signal is scoped to the one search it lands in; a batch driver treats the interrupted episode as a failed entry and continues with the next one.

import signal

import kd


def stop(signum, frame):
    raise kd.SearchInterrupted("wall-clock budget reached")


signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)
model = kd.Model(algorithm="sga", generations=200, seed=42)
try:
    model.fit(kd.load_kdv())
except kd.SearchInterrupted:
    pass  # the search stopped where the signal landed

docs.title: Surrogate models
docs.text:
kd.models moves a trained surrogate field model between processes as one file. Model.train_surrogate returns the trained module; save_field_model writes it under the kd-surrogate-v1 payload tag and load_field_model reads it back with the same torch_module_artifact digest, so a file written once can be injected into every segment of a lineage without the resume gate judging the model changed.

load_stored_surrogate reads the same file as a StoredSurrogate, the module plus the identity it was written with. For dlga, Model.train_surrogate(dataset, save_to=path) writes that identity (the dataset fingerprint, a SHA-256 of the whole training target field, the surrogate_* fields and the training seed; computed by kd.search.dlga_surrogate_identity), and Model(algorithm="dlga", surrogate_model=path) reads the file back and refuses it before the search if the fit's dataset or surrogate configuration is not the one it was trained on. The fit's seed need not be the training seed: one trained network serves searches under any seed. kd.search.save_dlga_surrogate / load_dlga_surrogate are the same pair outside the facade; load_dlga_surrogate also requires the training seed to match, since it answers which file a given configuration would have trained.

These names are imported from the subpackage rather than the package root: from kd.models import save_field_model, load_field_model.

Name Summary kd.models.save_field_model(model, path[, ...]) Write model as a kd-surrogate-v1 file and return its path. kd.models.load_field_model(path, device) Rebuild the FieldModel a kd-surrogate-v1 file describes. kd.models.load_stored_surrogate(path, device) Read a kd-surrogate-v1 file back as a StoredSurrogate. kd.models.StoredSurrogate(module, identity[, ...]) A kd-surrogate-v1 file read back: the module, the identity it was written with (None for a file written without one) and where it came from. kd.models.FieldRecipe(name, version[, ...]) The architecture and training settings of one field-network fit. kd.models.DLGA_NN_1 —

Attributes:

  • name (str) –

    Label of the recipe.

  • version (int) –

    Revision of the named recipe; a changed value under the same name is a different revision.

  • hidden_sizes (tuple[int, ...]) –

    FieldModel hidden-layer widths.

  • activation (Literal['tanh', 'sin', 'relu']) –

  • lr (float) –

    Adam learning rate of FieldModelTrainer.

  • max_epochs (int) –

    Epoch budget of FieldModelTrainer.fit.

  • patience (int | None) –

    Epochs without validation improvement before the fit stops; None trains the full budget.

  • val_ratio (float) –

    Fraction of the samples held out for validation.

  • restore_best (bool) –

    Whether the best validation epoch's weights are restored at the end of the fit.

  • training_dtype (TrainingDtype | None) –

    Precision FieldModelTrainer.fit computes in: None trains in the field's dtype, "float32" or "float64" names one; the trained network is returned in the field's dtype either way.

docs.title: Plot functions
docs.text:
kd.viz.plots draws one figure per function. Model.report and kd.VizEngine compose these functions into a report; a direct call draws a single figure without the engine. A function that draws on one Matplotlib axes accepts ax=None and then creates a styled figure of its own, or takes an Axes to place the panel in a figure the caller lays out. Most functions return a list of warnings; those that build their own figure return it together with the warnings.

plot_score_bar, plot_summary_table and render_overlaid_convergence take a list of results and draw one figure across runs. plot_field_comparison, plot_time_slices, plot_error_heatmap and the two animation functions take the forward integration of the discovered equation, which kd.viz.build_integration_result(result, dataset) computes. plot_plugin draws a named diagnostic panel of an algorithm. The figures a report contains, including each algorithm's panels, are listed under Visualization.

These names are imported from the subpackage rather than the package root: from kd.viz.plots import plot_convergence, plot_parity.

docs.text:
plot_field_comparison(
    dataset: PDEDataset,
    integration_result: IntegrationResult,
    *,
    style: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    field_cmap: FieldCmap = "sequential",
) -> tuple[Figure, list[str]]

Plot the observed field, the discovered law integrated, and their residual.

Panels: - Observed: dataset.fields[dataset.lhs_field].values (original physical field) - Discovered law, integrated: integration_result.predicted_field, the forward solution of the discovered equation (kd.viz.build_integration_result) - Residual: discovered - observed (positive = over-prediction)

1D spatial: pcolormesh over physical evolution/spatial coordinates 2D spatial: 2xN heatmap (3 selected time steps)

Without a predicted field the discovered panel shows the reason as text. The observed and discovered panels share one scale and one colorbar; the Residual panels share their own symmetric scale on the kd diverging map. A panel the shared scale clips carries a muted line under it with its actual range.

Parameters:

  • dataset (PDEDataset) –

    PDEDataset with field data and coordinates.

  • integration_result (IntegrationResult) –

    Integration result with predicted field.

  • style (dict[str, Any] | None, default: None ) –

    Optional matplotlib style overrides.

  • field_cmap (FieldCmap, default: 'sequential' ) –

    "sequential" (viridis) for the observed and discovered panels, or "diverging" (the kd diverging map, symmetric about zero) for two-phase fields.

Returns:

  • tuple[Figure, list[str]] –

    Tuple of (Figure, list of warnings).

docs.title: Recovery scores
docs.text:
When the governing equation is known, a run is judged on three axes at once: the term set, the coefficients, and the fit. judge_recovery returns that verdict from the data; judge_law compares the recovered terms and coefficients with the truth equation's without data, after reading the truth string with law_from_equation. term_set_jaccard and load_bearing_recall give partial credit beside the binary answer. Success rates over seeds are reported with a Wilson interval and compared pairwise with an exact test, so a rate on this site or in a report always carries its uncertainty.

Name Summary kd.judge_recovery(rhs, u_t[, ...]) Judge one reconstructed RHS against a known truth law, numerically. kd.RecoveryVerdict(structure_ok, coefficients_ok[, ...]) Three-axis aggregate recovery judgment (charter §5.4-3, projection form). kd.span_floor(u_t, truth_columns) Oracle B: the best NMSE reachable inside the truth span, plus its fit. kd.term_set_jaccard(actual, truth) Jaccard similarity of two term-label sets: kd.load_bearing_recall(verdict, nmse_threshold) Share of truth terms the reconstruction individually depends on. kd.judge_law(terms, coefficients[, ...]) Judge a candidate law against a truth law, term by term and without data. kd.TermVerdict(structure_ok, coefficients_ok[, ...]) Term-level verdict of a candidate law against a truth law. kd.law_from_equation(equation, axes[, ...]) Read a truth equation string into a ParsedLaw. kd.ParsedLaw(lhs, terms[, ...]) A truth equation read into monomial labels and their coefficients. kd.wilson_interval(successes, trials[, ...]) Wilson score interval for a binomial proportion. kd.rate_summary(successes, trials[, ...]) successes / trials with its Wilson interval, as one record. kd.RateSummary(successes, trials[, ...]) One benchmark cell's rate, ready for a report row. kd.paired_exact_test(only_a, only_b) Two-sided exact McNemar p-value on the discordant pairs.

docs.title: Plugin interfaces
docs.text:
kd.search holds the machinery behind the algorithm plugins; this page lists the part a plugin author implements, a mode-routing helper, and the record of a run with a reader for its event log. SurrogateTrainer is the protocol an algorithm whose descriptor names config_artifact_keys must satisfy, a train_surrogate method and an artifacts mapping; a registry-level test enforces the pairing for every registered algorithm.

mode_inputs projects a DatasetReport.to_dict() onto the arguments of kd.mode_accepts, so whether a mode of an algorithm accepts a dataset can be decided from the dataset's report and the published schema alone. RunRecord is the sealed record of one run: its cost, the deterministic evidence, the run specification and the hashes that bind them. last_completed_iteration reads the last completed iteration from a run directory's events.jsonl, including one left by a run that was killed while writing.

These names are imported from the subpackage rather than the package root: from kd.search import SurrogateTrainer.

docs.title: read_run_state
docs.text:
read_run_state(run_dir: Path | str) -> RunState

Return the state a run directory records for its run.

Three limits of what a directory can say:

  • A process killed outright writes nothing more, so its directory keeps reading preparing or running, exactly like a fit still at work. Whoever started the process knows whether it is alive; the directory does not. An ended process whose directory reads preparing or running was killed.
  • A stop by a budget (max_seconds) or by a callback is not an exception: the fit returns and seals a record, so the state is completed and the record's cost.stop_reason names the stop.
  • The error is recorded only where phase lines are: with phase lines off (RecordingOptions(phases=False)) a raised episode reads failed from its manifest, with no stage and no error. Without phase lines and without a manifest, events.jsonl existing is what says running.

Raises:

  • FileNotFoundError –

    If run_dir is not a directory.

  • ValueError –

    If manifest.json is not a kd run-directory manifest, or the last phase line is not a kd-runphase-v1 line.

docs.title: RunState dataclass
docs.text:
What a run directory says about its run (read_run_state).

Attributes:

  • state (Literal['preparing', 'running', 'completed', 'failed', 'interrupted']) –

    "preparing" (no search loop yet), "running" (search loop started), "completed" (the search loop ended, or the directory is sealed completed / no_record), "failed" (the fit raised) or "interrupted" (the fit raised a KeyboardInterrupt or a kd.SearchInterrupted: someone stopped it).

  • sealed (bool) –

    Whether the run-level manifest.json exists. Record, recorder and manifest are written after the search loop ends, so completed with sealed=False is a fit that is still building its result, or one whose caller never sealed the directory.

  • stage (str | None) –

    For failed / interrupted, where the fit was: setup (before fit_started), prepare (before the search loop), search or finalize (after the loop). None when the directory does not say.

  • error_type (str | None) –

    The exception class's qualified name, when recorded.

  • error_message (str | None) –

    The exception's message as the failure line stores it (environment credentials replaced by [redacted:NAME], cut to 2000 characters), when recorded.

docs.text:
evaluate_terms(
    dataset: PDEDataset,
    terms: Sequence[str],
    *,
    skip_invalid: bool = False,
    max_order: int = 2,
    lhs_order: int | None = None,
    rows: Tensor | None = None,
    fixed: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    sketch: Sketch | SketchSpec | None = None,
) -> EvaluationResult

Evaluate candidate terms against a dataset, fail-loud.

Parameters:

  • dataset (PDEDataset) –

    The PDE dataset to evaluate against (never mutated).

  • terms (Sequence[str]) –

    Candidate term strings (canonical funcall IR or product notation). result.terms keeps the caller's spelling and order.

  • skip_invalid (bool, default: False ) –

    When False (default, strict), ANY rejected term raises InvalidTermsError carrying every rejection and nothing is fitted. When True (lenient), rejected terms are dropped with exactly one logger.warning and the survivors are fitted.

  • max_order (int, default: 2 ) –

    Maximum atomic derivative order (-> max_atomic_order).

  • lhs_order (int | None, default: None ) –

    LHS derivative order targeted by the fit (1 -> u_t, 2 -> u_tt; -> DerivativeReqs.lhs_order). Default None DERIVES from dataset.lhs_order (single source of truth).

  • rows (Tensor | None, default: None ) –

    Grid-shaped boolean mask or flat int32/int64 sample indices. Derivatives and term validation run on the complete grid first.

  • fixed (Mapping[str, float] | None, default: None ) –

    Term to coefficient for terms whose coefficient is held, not fitted. Keys are written as terms are (u*u_x and mul(u,u_x) fix one column).

  • sketch (Sketch | SketchSpec | None, default: None ) –

    A kd.Sketch whose pinned terms are the fixed coefficients; its anchored terms and holes do not change the fit.

Returns:

  • EvaluationResult –

    An EvaluationResult with is_valid is True (honest metrics).

  • EvaluationResult –

    This entry always measures condition_number (candidate-library

  • EvaluationResult –

    collinearity). The measured matrix is the one the solver was handed:

  • EvaluationResult –

    under skip_invalid=True that is the SURVIVING columns, not every

  • EvaluationResult –

    string in terms — a term dropped as shape / all-zero /

  • EvaluationResult –

    tautology is not in the number. Strict mode fits every submitted

  • EvaluationResult –

    term or raises, so there the two coincide. Under fixed coefficients

  • EvaluationResult –

    it is the matrix of the fitted (free) columns, None when every term

  • EvaluationResult –

    is fixed; complexity and score count the free columns.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If terms is empty.

  • ValueError –

    Propagated from PlatformBuilder when the resolved LHS field/axis is absent from the dataset, when the resolved lhs_order > max_order (the LHS is read from the same precomputed derivative cache that max_order bounds), or when max_order > 3 (provider cap).

  • ValueError –

    A refused fixed or sketch (see those arguments).

  • InvalidTermsError –

    If terms are rejected (see skip_invalid), or an input term cannot be fitted beside the fixed terms.

  • EvaluationFailedError –

    If the final fit is invalid (the penalty sentinel is never returned).

Parameters:

  • terms (Sequence[str]) –

  • coefficients (Sequence[float]) –

  • method (str, default: 'Radau' ) –

  • max_seconds (float | None, default: None ) –

    Wall-clock budget in seconds; None sets no limit.

Returns:

docs.title: ForwardError dataclass
docs.text:
Outcome of forward_error.

Attributes:

  • value (float | None) –

    ||pred - u||_2 / ||u||_2 over the full grid, or None when the equation could not be integrated or was not measured.

  • reason (str | None) –

    None when value is set; otherwise "diverged", "solve-failed" (scipy solve_ivp failed), "refused" (the equation or dataset is unsupported) or "timeout" (the max_seconds deadline passed: unmeasured, not a numerical outcome).

  • warning (str) –

    Why integration was refused, failed or stopped, empty on a clean run.

  • terms (tuple[str, ...]) –

    The submitted terms.

  • coefficients (tuple[float, ...]) –

    The submitted coefficients, one per term.

  • input_identity (str | None) –

    compute_dataset_fingerprint of the comparison input with its LHS defaults resolved.

  • interval (tuple[float, float] | None) –

    (t_first, t_last) of the integration, None when the input is not a grid.

  • boundary (Mapping[str, str] | None) –

    Per spatial axis, "periodic" or "held_initial" (both endpoints held at their initial values); None when the input is not a grid.

    If a law's terms and coefficients differ in length or a coefficient is non-finite (the message names the law), rtol, atol or max_seconds is not a positive finite number, the observed states are zero everywhere, or the error is non-finite.

    An external stop or an allocation failure inside the integration propagates.

docs.title: refit_terms
docs.text:
refit_terms(
    dataset: PDEDataset,
    terms: Sequence[str],
    coefficients: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    *,
    small_term_rtol: float = 0.0,
    lhs_order: int | None = None,
    max_order: int = 3,
    method: str = "finite_diff",
    trim: Trim = 0,
    rows: Tensor | None = None,
    surrogate: StoredSurrogate | None = None,
    weak: WeakFormOptions | None = None,
    fixed: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    sketch: Sketch | SketchSpec | None = None,
) -> RefitResult

Prune small terms by their input coefficients, then refit the rest once.

Parameters:

  • dataset (PDEDataset) –

    The PDE dataset to fit against (never mutated).

  • terms (Sequence[str]) –

    Candidate terms in canonical funcall IR or product notation, as in evaluate_terms; result.terms and result.dropped keep the caller's spelling.

  • coefficients (Sequence[float] | None, default: None ) –

    One input coefficient per term, used only for pruning; required when small_term_rtol > 0.

  • small_term_rtol (float, default: 0.0 ) –

    Relative pruning tolerance in [0, 1).

  • lhs_order (int | None, default: None ) –

    As in evaluate_terms; None takes dataset.lhs_order.

  • max_order (int, default: 3 ) –

    As in evaluate_terms. The default 3 keeps third-order terminal tokens such as u_xxx resolvable.

  • method (str, default: 'finite_diff' ) –

    A registered name from kd.refit_methods(); built-ins are "finite_diff", "autograd", "weak" and "fd2".

  • trim (Trim, default: 0 ) –

    0 (default), a nonnegative integer, a mapping from axis name to a nonnegative integer, or "by_order". Not with autograd as "by_order" (no stencils).

  • rows (Tensor | None, default: None ) –

    Grid-shaped boolean mask or flat integer sample indices.

  • surrogate (StoredSurrogate | None, default: None ) –

    The stored surrogate autograd differentiates (kd.models.load_stored_surrogate); refused by other methods.

  • weak (WeakFormOptions | None, default: None ) –

    WeakFormOptions for method="weak" (None takes the defaults: automatic widths, no correction); refused otherwise.

  • fixed (Mapping[str, float] | None, default: None ) –

    Term to fixed coefficient; see evaluate_terms.

  • sketch (Sketch | SketchSpec | None, default: None ) –

    A kd.Sketch whose pinned terms are the fixed coefficients; see evaluate_terms. A shorthand Sketch binds to the LHS at the resolved lhs_order.

Returns:

  • RefitResult –

    A RefitResult with mse and frame set, and weak for a weak fit.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If small_term_rtol is outside [0, 1) (NaN included), if coefficients is given with a length other than len(terms) (at any tolerance), or if small_term_rtol > 0 without coefficients.

  • NotImplementedError –

    As in evaluate_terms: a tabular dataset or a resolved LHS order of 0; only grid datasets with a first- or second-order LHS are fitted. Under weak: a term outside the class or an unsupported dataset (see method).

  • EvaluationFailedError –

    The final fit is invalid (weak: the SVD did not converge).

Two spellings of one column (mul(u,u_x) and mul(u_x,u)) are two exactly collinear columns: the fit returns the minimum-norm split between them with condition_number infinite, as evaluate_terms does.

docs.title: from_sympy
docs.text:
from_sympy(expr: Expr) -> str

Serialize a supported SymPy expression into kd function-call IR.

Supported subset

Symbol / Integer / Float / Rational / Add / Mul / integer and half-integer Pow / diff_* (single argument) / sin / cos / exp / log / lap. sqrt(x) is Pow(x, 1/2) in SymPy and serializes as sqrt(x); Pow(x, -1/2) as recip(sqrt(x)); any other Pow(x, p/2) as the integer power p of sqrt(x) (for example x**(3/2) as n3(sqrt(x))). A Float exponent whose value is exactly an integer or half-integer (x**0.5, x**2.0) serializes as the power with that Rational exponent.

Anything outside this subset -- other fractional powers (x**(1/3), x**(3/4)), symbolic exponents (x**x), other Float exponents (x**0.3), Abs, Min / Max, Piecewise, or an unknown Function -- raises ValueError. There is no silent degradation: an unrepresentable expression is a hard failure so callers never receive a lossy approximation.

Caveat -- operator-name collisions: a Symbol whose name matches a kd IR function (add / mul / div / n2 / n3 / recip / sin / cos / exp / log / sqrt / lap / diff_*) serializes to that bare token, which the kd parser then reads as an operator rather than a variable -- silently changing meaning or failing downstream. Callers must keep symbol names disjoint from kd operator names (kd-internal callers are safe: variable names come from the term library).

Round-trip preserves supported expressions semantically except when they contain a non-integer Rational that is not exactly representable as a binary float. Non-integer Rationals serialize as one Float literal: exact for values such as 1/2 and 3/4, approximate for values such as 1/3. This keeps the output executable because div(int, int) violates the kd executor's Tensor-only safe-division contract. The serializer also orders Add / Mul by SymPy canonical order, so the exact IR string is not guaranteed (e.g. div(u, x) round-trips to mul(u, recip(x))). SymPy also merges half powers, so n2(sqrt(u)) round-trips to u, which is finite where the original column is NaN (u < 0).

Parameters:

  • expr (Expr) –

    A SymPy expression in the supported subset.

Returns:

  • str –

    The kd function-call IR string.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If expr contains a construct outside the supported subset.

docs.title: ODE trajectories
docs.text:
kd.data holds the containers for ODE observations and the functions that turn them into regression tables. A Trajectory is one time series with its own strictly increasing time points, the states sampled at them and the known parameter values; a TrajectorySet groups the trajectories of one system under shared state and parameter names. generate_ode_trajectories integrates a set for one of the systems in kd.data.ODE_SYSTEMS.

Model.fit takes a PDEDataset or a TabularDataset, so a set is prepared with prepare_trajectory_regression, which differentiates each trajectory separately, and the returned TrajectoryRegression is projected to one table per target state. The workflow is described under ODE trajectories.

These names are imported from the subpackage rather than the package root: from kd.data import TrajectorySet, prepare_trajectory_regression.

Name Summary kd.data.Trajectory(id, t[, ...]) One trajectory of a system. kd.data.TrajectorySet(name, source[, ...]) Trajectories of one system. kd.data.generate_ode_trajectories(system, seed[, ...]) Integrate n_trajectories trajectories of system from initial states drawn with numpy.random.default_rng(seed). kd.data.prepare_trajectory_regression(trajectories, derivatives[, ...]) Materialize all state derivatives, independently for each trajectory. kd.data.TrajectoryRegression(metadata, arrays[, ...]) Owned numeric preprocessing result, produced by prepare/load helpers. kd.data.TrajectoryNNConfig(seed, hidden_sizes[, ...]) Per-trajectory FieldModel training; no search settings or shared seed. kd.data.derivative_target(state) The regression target of state's time derivative: d<state>_dt. kd.data.trajectories_to_tabular(trajectories, target_state[, ...]) The regression table of target_state's time derivative. kd.data.save_trajectory_regression(result, directory) Save numeric arrays, recipe, reports and already requested projections. kd.data.load_trajectory_regression(directory) Load and verify a numeric bundle without a network or derivative call.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
kd.VizEngine renders the figures of a fitted run into a directory and writes an HTML report that embeds them. Model.report(output_dir) runs the same pass with the result, the algorithm and the dataset of that fit, and returns a ReportResult listing the figure paths, the report path and a warning for each figure that was skipped or degraded. The report and the panels each algorithm adds are described under Visualization; the functions that draw one figure each are listed under Plot functions.

kd.preview and kd.preview_report inspect a dataset before a fit and draw nothing. preview prints a text summary of the axes, the fields and the left-hand side; preview_report returns the same facts as a DatasetReport, with three per-field diagnostics that preview does not print.

docs.title: Bundled datasets
docs.text: KD ships a catalog of benchmark datasets with known equations, so you can try an algorithm out before pointing it at data of your own, and two sets of laboratory measurements to run against real data.

docs.title: Load a dataset
docs.text:
Each dataset has a convenience loader that hands back an object fit() accepts directly:

import kd

dataset = kd.load_burgers()
print(dataset.name, dataset.get_shape())

burgers (256, 201)

You can also go through the catalog by id. kd.list_datasets() returns every entry, and kd.get_dataset(id) returns one entry's metadata: the equation, the axes, the left-hand side, the file format, the source, the license, and a pointer to its loader. The data itself arrives only when you call spec.loader().

import kd

spec = kd.get_dataset("kdv")
print(spec.id, spec.tier, spec.axes, spec.lhs)

dataset = spec.loader()
print(dataset.name, dataset.get_shape())

kdv builtin ('x', 't') u_t
kdv (256, 201)

docs.title: Bundled and downloaded datasets
docs.text:
Entries come in two kinds, recorded in the tier field:

  • builtin: the data file is installed with the package, and loading it touches no network.
  • remote: the file is fetched from the Hugging Face Hub the first time you load it. The fetch is pinned to a fixed file at a fixed revision and verified against a recorded sha256; a mismatch deletes the cached copy and raises. Once verified, the file stays in the local cache and later loads read it from there.

kd.list_remote_datasets() lists only the remote ones. kd.load_from_hub(dataset_id, cache_dir=..., offline=...) loads a remote dataset by id, with cache_dir choosing where the cache lives and offline=True restricting it to files already cached.

For the shape requirements and the left-hand-side spec, see data requirements.
